title: Lesson 10: Genetic Programming, Artificial Life, and Swarm Intelligence

slides.title: Can a computer search over programs—not just numbers?

segments.label: Concept
segments.text: Lesson ten asks what changes when the candidate solution is itself a program. In ordinary genetic algorithms, a chromosome may encode numbers or a fixed route. Genetic programming, or GP, evolves executable structure. The individuals are little programs that can run, fail, surprise us, and occasionally behave like an intern who discovered recursion before discovering comments.

focuses.label: Concept

segments.label: Mechanism
segments.text: The driving question has four verbs: represent, execute, score, and vary. We need a language for candidate programs, an interpreter that runs them, a fitness function that evaluates behavior, and operators that change program structure without producing nonsense. Selection then makes useful partial programs more likely to survive and recombine.

segments.label: Example and metaphor
segments.text: The lesson broadens from GP to artificial life and swarm intelligence. Artificial life asks which life-like processes become visible when we construct systems. Swarm methods ask how local rules and shared signals create organized global behavior. The unifying idea is emergence: complex results can grow from repeated simple interactions.

segments.label: Boundary
segments.text: Use a recipe metaphor carefully. A fixed chromosome is like a list of ingredient quantities; a GP individual is closer to the entire recipe, including conditional steps and loops. Changing one subtree can replace a whole cooking procedure. That flexibility expands the search space and makes validity, cost, and interpretability central design problems.

segments.label: Transfer and audit
segments.text: By the end, you should be able to contrast GA and GP representations, trace program-tree generation, explain subtree mutation and crossover, design a maze fitness function, and distinguish PSO, bee recruitment, and ant pheromone memory. The goal is not to memorize animal mascots. It is to identify representation, feedback, and state in each algorithm.

slides.title: Genetic programming evolves executable structures

segments.label: Concept
segments.text: The definition has three cards. A candidate is an executable program, not merely a parameter vector. Its quality can only be judged after execution on tasks or examples. That means evaluation may be expensive, noisy, unsafe, or capable of timing out, so the runtime environment becomes part of the optimization problem.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: The definition has three cards. A candidate

focuses.phrase: The definition has three cards. A candidate
focuses.label: Concept

segments.label: Mechanism
segments.text: The representation is usually a parse tree whose size and shape can change. Internal nodes are functions and leaves are terminals. Unlike a fixed twenty-two-bit chromosome, two program trees may contain different numbers of nodes. Variable length lets GP discover structure, but it also creates the danger of uncontrolled growth called bloat.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: The representation is usually a parse tree

focuses.phrase: The representation is usually a parse tree
focuses.label: Mechanism

kinetics.phrase: The representation is usually a parse tree
kinetics.label: Candidate programs and variable trees

segments.label: Example and metaphor
segments.text: The search mechanism remains evolutionary: initialize programs, execute and score them, select parents, apply program-aware variation, and update the population. GP is therefore not a different universe from GA. It is the same outer evolutionary contract with a representation that carries syntax, control, and executable meaning.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: The search mechanism remains evolutionary: initialize programs,

focuses.phrase: The search mechanism remains evolutionary: initialize programs,
focuses.label: Example and metaphor

segments.label: Boundary
segments.text: A useful boundary: evolving source text character by character is technically possible but usually gives terrible neighborhoods. Most random edits break syntax, and small textual changes may have arbitrary effects. Tree or grammar representations bias variation toward structurally valid programs. Representation supplies the search with a usable grammar.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: A useful boundary: evolving source text character

focuses.phrase: A useful boundary: evolving source text character
focuses.label: Boundary

segments.label: Transfer and audit
segments.text: Ask the three-card audit on any GP claim. What exactly executes? How is it represented? What evidence determines reproduction? If a paper says programs evolved but never specifies these three items, the method description has the nutritional value of a menu that says only, 'food happened.'

visualDesign.focusPhrase: Ask the three-card audit on any GP

focuses.phrase: Ask the three-card audit on any GP
focuses.label: Transfer and audit

slides.title: Lisp makes hierarchical program structure visible

segments.label: Concept
segments.text: Lisp places a function before its arguments. In the displayed prefix expression, the outer plus is the root call. The values two and three are direct arguments, while the multiplication and division expressions are nested arguments that become complete child subtrees.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: Lisp places a function before its arguments.

focuses.phrase: Lisp places a function before its arguments.
focuses.label: Concept

segments.label: Mechanism
segments.text: Parentheses make hierarchy explicit. Read an opening parenthesis, then a function, then the arguments required by that function. Nested parentheses mean evaluate a child call before passing its result upward. Lisp is the source example's language; genetic programming itself is not restricted to Lisp.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: Parentheses make hierarchy explicit. Read an opening

focuses.phrase: Parentheses make hierarchy explicit. Read an opening
focuses.label: Mechanism

kinetics.phrase: Parentheses make hierarchy explicit. Read an opening
kinetics.label: Prefix syntax exposes the tree

segments.label: Example and metaphor
segments.text: The slide defines three terms. A function is an operator with argument positions. A terminal is a variable, constant, sensor, or action with no children. A parse tree records the hierarchical evaluation structure connecting those functions and terminals.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: The slide defines three terms. A function

focuses.phrase: The slide defines three terms. A function
focuses.label: Example and metaphor

segments.label: Boundary
segments.text: Prefix notation is convenient because there is no ambiguity about precedence. The tree and expression carry the same computation. Translation between them should be testable in both directions: parse text into a tree, then serialize the tree and confirm that evaluation stays equivalent.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: Prefix notation is convenient because there is

focuses.phrase: Prefix notation is convenient because there is
focuses.label: Boundary

segments.label: Transfer and audit
segments.text: Do not mistake readable syntax for a good search space. Lisp can express the tree cleanly, but designers must still choose safe primitives, arities, types, depth limits, and fitness. Parentheses organize the guests; they do not guarantee the dinner conversation is productive.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: Do not mistake readable syntax for a

focuses.phrase: Do not mistake readable syntax for a
focuses.label: Transfer and audit

slides.title: The program text and tree encode the same computation

segments.label: Concept
segments.text: Read the displayed tree from its leaves upward. Internal nodes come from the function set: addition, subtraction, multiplication, and protected division. Each function has an arity, the number of children it requires. A binary plus node is incomplete until it has two child programs.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: Read the displayed tree from its leaves

focuses.phrase: Read the displayed tree from its leaves
focuses.label: Concept

segments.label: Mechanism
segments.text: Leaves come from the terminal set: constants such as two, three, seven, and five, plus variables X and Y. Terminals end recursion because they require no child expressions. When a variable leaf executes, its value comes from the current input case; a constant supplies the same value every time.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: Leaves come from the terminal set: constants

focuses.phrase: Leaves come from the terminal set: constants
focuses.label: Mechanism

kinetics.phrase: Leaves come from the terminal set: constants
kinetics.label: Text and parse tree are equivalent
kinetics.text: Text and parse tree are equivalent

segments.label: Example and metaphor
segments.text: The tree encodes a prefix-style expression. Execution recursively evaluates children and sends their results to the parent function. This makes the tree both data and a program. It is a blueprint that can be traversed, copied, replaced, and executed without first flattening it into a line of text.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: The tree encodes a prefix-style expression. Execution

focuses.phrase: The tree encodes a prefix-style expression. Execution
focuses.label: Example and metaphor

segments.label: Boundary
segments.text: Protected division illustrates closure. Ordinary division can fail at zero. GP often defines protected division to return a safe fallback when the denominator is zero. Then any generated tree composed from the primitive set can run. We change the operator slightly so evolution cannot discover that crashing is a creative answer.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: Protected division illustrates closure. Ordinary division can

focuses.phrase: Protected division illustrates closure. Ordinary division can
focuses.label: Boundary

segments.label: Transfer and audit
segments.text: Before running GP, test the primitive set independently. Verify arity, types, boundary behavior, and execution limits. The search will combine primitives in arrangements no human would volunteer to write. If one primitive is unsafe, evolution will eventually find the unsafe corner with the persistence of a toddler testing cabinet locks.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: Before running GP, test the primitive set

focuses.phrase: Before running GP, test the primitive set
focuses.label: Transfer and audit

slides.title: Initialize, evaluate, select, vary, replace, and repeat

segments.label: Concept
segments.text: Begin with random programs. Each tree must obey the grammar, depth constraints, and type rules. Random generation should create structural diversity without filling the population with programs so enormous that the first evaluation finishes during the next academic catalog cycle.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: Begin with random programs. Each tree must

focuses.phrase: Begin with random programs. Each tree must
focuses.label: Concept

segments.label: Mechanism
segments.text: Execute every program on the evaluation cases and compute fitness. Fitness may reward prediction accuracy, navigation success, low resource use, or a combination. If behavior is stochastic, repeat trials or share scenarios so lucky programs do not receive a hereditary title.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: Execute every program on the evaluation cases

focuses.phrase: Execute every program on the evaluation cases
focuses.label: Mechanism

kinetics.phrase: Execute every program on the evaluation cases
kinetics.label: The complete GP control contract

segments.label: Example and metaphor
segments.text: Selection chooses programs to reproduce. Subtree crossover exchanges components between parents; subtree mutation replaces one component with a new random subtree. These operators preserve syntactic structure when they cut at node boundaries, but they do not automatically preserve good behavior.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: Selection chooses programs to reproduce. Subtree crossover

focuses.phrase: Selection chooses programs to reproduce. Subtree crossover
focuses.label: Example and metaphor

segments.label: Boundary
segments.text: Create the new population using a generational or steady-state replacement policy. Elitism can preserve the best known program, while diversity mechanisms prevent one family from monopolizing the population. The population is a portfolio of executable hypotheses, not merely a queue waiting behind the current champion.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: Create the new population using a generational

focuses.phrase: Create the new population using a generational
focuses.label: Boundary

segments.label: Transfer and audit
segments.text: Check termination after a target fitness, evaluation budget, generation limit, or lack of improvement. Return the best supported program and report its held-out performance, size, and cost. A long family tree is evidence of compute spent, not proof that the final descendant is optimal.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: Check termination after a target fitness, evaluation

focuses.phrase: Check termination after a target fitness, evaluation
focuses.label: Transfer and audit

slides.title: Fitness guides reproduction; operators create the next programs

segments.label: Concept
segments.text: The lifecycle begins with random programs, then executes and scores every individual. Selection samples parents using fitness evidence. Variation edits or recombines their trees, and the resulting valid offspring fill a complete new population P prime.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: The lifecycle begins with random programs, then

focuses.phrase: The lifecycle begins with random programs, then
focuses.label: Concept

segments.label: Mechanism
segments.text: Fitness guides reproductive probability; it does not directly edit code. A high score increases sampling opportunity, while crossover and mutation perform the structural changes. Keeping those roles separate prevents the common explanation that fitness somehow reaches into a tree and repairs it.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: Fitness guides reproductive probability; it does not

focuses.phrase: Fitness guides reproductive probability; it does not
focuses.label: Mechanism

kinetics.phrase: Fitness guides reproductive probability; it does not
kinetics.label: One complete GP population cycle

segments.label: Example and metaphor
segments.text: Replacement determines whether the whole parent generation disappears, whether elites survive, or whether updates occur continuously. The diagram shows a generational cycle: complete P prime, assign it as the new P, evaluate, and repeat.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: Replacement determines whether the whole parent generation

focuses.phrase: Replacement determines whether the whole parent generation
focuses.label: Example and metaphor

segments.label: Boundary
segments.text: The stop decision may use target performance, evaluation budget, generation limit, or stalled improvement. A yes exits with the best supported program. A no returns to the cycle. Stopping is evidence policy, not a tiny finish-line flag discovered inside the tree.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: The stop decision may use target performance,

focuses.phrase: The stop decision may use target performance,
focuses.label: Boundary

segments.label: Transfer and audit
segments.text: Audit one loop by following a single useful subtree. It appears in a parent, wins reproductive opportunity, survives a legal operator, enters P prime, and receives a new score in context. That trace explains cumulative search more clearly than a cloud of animated family-tree arrows.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: Audit one loop by following a single

focuses.phrase: Audit one loop by following a single

slides.title: Function and terminal sets define what GP can build

segments.label: Concept
segments.text: The function set contains plus, minus, multiplication, and protected division. Every function declares an arity. Choosing a binary function creates two open child positions that recursive generation must fill.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: The function set contains plus, minus, multiplication,

focuses.phrase: The function set contains plus, minus, multiplication,
focuses.label: Concept

segments.label: Mechanism
segments.text: The terminal set contains integers, X, and Y. A terminal closes a branch because it needs no children. Variables receive values from the current task input, while constants supply fixed numeric material.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: The terminal set contains integers, X, and

focuses.phrase: The terminal set contains integers, X, and
focuses.label: Mechanism

kinetics.phrase: The terminal set contains integers, X, and
kinetics.label: The GP grammar contract

segments.label: Example and metaphor
segments.text: The validity rule combines membership and arity: internal nodes come from the function set, leaves come from the terminal set, and each function receives exactly its required arguments. That rule is a grammar for executable candidates.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: The validity rule combines membership and arity:

focuses.phrase: The validity rule combines membership and arity:
focuses.label: Example and metaphor

segments.label: Boundary
segments.text: Sufficiency asks whether this grammar can express a solution. Closure asks whether every legal combination can execute. Protected division supports closure by defining safe behavior at a zero denominator instead of letting evolution submit a crash report as a candidate.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: Sufficiency asks whether this grammar can express

focuses.phrase: Sufficiency asks whether this grammar can express
focuses.label: Boundary

segments.label: Transfer and audit
segments.text: Primitive design embeds domain knowledge and bias. Too few primitives exclude useful programs; too many create an enormous, redundant search space. The toolbox should contain what the job needs, not every object found in the garage after midnight.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: Primitive design embeds domain knowledge and bias.

focuses.phrase: Primitive design embeds domain knowledge and bias.
focuses.label: Transfer and audit

slides.title: Random generation recursively fills every argument position

segments.label: Concept
segments.text: The interactive builder starts with an incomplete root expression. Program generation is recursive: choose either a function or terminal where a node is needed. Choosing a function creates new child positions; choosing a terminal closes that branch.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: The interactive builder starts with an incomplete

focuses.phrase: The interactive builder starts with an incomplete
focuses.label: Concept

segments.label: Mechanism
segments.text: A full method forces functions until a minimum depth and then places terminals at the boundary. A grow method allows functions or terminals earlier, producing varied shapes. Ramped half-and-half mixes methods and depth limits to create a more diverse initial population.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: A full method forces functions until a

focuses.phrase: A full method forces functions until a
focuses.label: Mechanism

kinetics.phrase: A full method forces functions until a
kinetics.label: Recursive program generation

segments.label: Example and metaphor
segments.text: Every choice must respect arity. If we place multiplication, two child expressions are required. If we place X or five, recursion stops at that leaf. The generator is like assembling a legal sentence from grammar rules: creativity is welcome, but verbs cannot wander off without their required arguments.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: Every choice must respect arity. If we

focuses.phrase: Every choice must respect arity. If we
focuses.label: Example and metaphor

segments.label: Boundary
segments.text: Depth and node limits control resource use. Without them, recursive generation can create huge trees before fitness has evaluated anything. Limits are search biases: they exclude some programs, but they make evaluation feasible and reduce the chance that size alone consumes the experiment.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: Depth and node limits control resource use.

focuses.phrase: Depth and node limits control resource use.
focuses.label: Boundary

segments.label: Transfer and audit
segments.text: As we advance the builder, track which positions are still open. A program is executable only when every function has all required children and every branch ends in a terminal. The final tree is one candidate, not a guarantee that its arithmetic is useful.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: As we advance the builder, track which

focuses.phrase: As we advance the builder, track which
focuses.label: Transfer and audit

segments.label: Builder state 2
segments.text: Choose generation step two. Terminal two fills the first open argument of the root plus. The branch closes because a terminal has no children, while other root arguments remain open.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: Choose generation step two. Terminal two fills

focuses.phrase: Choose generation step two. Terminal two fills
focuses.label: Builder state 2

segments.label: Builder state 3
segments.text: Choose generation step three. Terminal three fills the next root argument. The partial expression is legal but incomplete; every remaining function position still needs a recursively generated child.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: Choose generation step three. Terminal three fills

focuses.phrase: Choose generation step three. Terminal three fills
focuses.label: Builder state 3

segments.label: Builder state 4
segments.text: Choose generation step four. Multiplication becomes a nested function. Selecting a function creates new argument obligations, so the generator must later supply both operands before this branch can execute.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: Choose generation step four. Multiplication becomes a

focuses.phrase: Choose generation step four. Multiplication becomes a
focuses.label: Builder state 4

segments.label: Builder state 5
segments.text: Choose generation step five. Division is added and the multiplication branch receives X and seven. The hot node marks the newest structural choice, while division still contains open positions.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: Choose generation step five. Division is added

focuses.phrase: Choose generation step five. Division is added
focuses.label: Builder state 5

segments.label: Builder state 6
segments.text: Choose generation step six. Y and five close the division branch. Every function now has its required children and every path ends in a terminal, producing a syntactically complete executable program.

focuses.phrase: Choose generation step six. Y and five

slides.title: Mutation replaces one selected subtree with a random program

segments.label: Concept
segments.text: Mutation begins by selecting a node in one parent tree. That node represents the root of a complete subprogram. Delete the selected subtree, generate a replacement that satisfies grammar and depth constraints, and splice it into the same position.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: Mutation begins by selecting a node in

focuses.phrase: Mutation begins by selecting a node in
focuses.label: Concept

segments.label: Mechanism
segments.text: Selecting a leaf makes a small structural change, such as replacing X with a constant. Selecting a node near the root can replace most of the program. Mutation severity therefore depends on selection depth and replacement size, not merely on a single probability.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: Selecting a leaf makes a small structural

focuses.phrase: Selecting a leaf makes a small structural
focuses.label: Mechanism

kinetics.phrase: Selecting a leaf makes a small structural
kinetics.label: Subtree mutation

segments.label: Example and metaphor
segments.text: The new subtree may improve, harm, or leave fitness unchanged. Neutral mutations can still matter because they alter structure available for future crossover. However, repeated neutral additions may cause bloat, where programs grow without corresponding behavioral improvement.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: The new subtree may improve, harm, or

focuses.phrase: The new subtree may improve, harm, or
focuses.label: Example and metaphor

segments.label: Boundary
segments.text: A type-aware system must ensure the replacement returns the value expected at that position. An arithmetic expression cannot be replaced with a robot action unless the language defines how those types interact. Strongly typed GP turns semantic categories into enforceable constraints.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: A type-aware system must ensure the replacement

focuses.phrase: A type-aware system must ensure the replacement
focuses.label: Boundary

segments.label: Transfer and audit
segments.text: Mutation introduces novel structure that may not exist in either parent. It is the evolutionary equivalent of renovating one room without demolishing the whole house. Occasionally the contractor replaces the kitchen with a trampoline; fitness then decides whether that innovation reproduces.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: Mutation introduces novel structure that may not

focuses.phrase: Mutation introduces novel structure that may not
focuses.label: Transfer and audit

slides.title: Crossover swaps subtrees between two parent programs

segments.label: Concept
segments.text: Crossover selects one node in each parent. Each selected node defines a complete subtree. Swap those subtrees to create offspring. Cutting at node boundaries preserves syntax because every moved object is already a valid subprogram.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: Crossover selects one node in each parent.

focuses.phrase: Crossover selects one node in each parent.
focuses.label: Concept

segments.label: Mechanism
segments.text: The operator transmits building blocks: a useful arithmetic transformation, condition, or navigation routine can move into a different context. But context changes meaning. A subtree that helps beneath multiplication may be harmful beneath division, so syntactic validity does not imply semantic compatibility.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: The operator transmits building blocks: a useful

focuses.phrase: The operator transmits building blocks: a useful
focuses.label: Mechanism

kinetics.phrase: The operator transmits building blocks: a useful
kinetics.label: Subtree crossover

segments.label: Example and metaphor
segments.text: Depth limits may reject a swap if the inserted subtree makes an offspring too deep. Size-fair crossover tries to exchange similarly sized material, reducing bloat. Typed crossover restricts swaps to subtrees with compatible return types.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: Depth limits may reject a swap if

focuses.phrase: Depth limits may reject a swap if
focuses.label: Example and metaphor

segments.label: Boundary
segments.text: Compare this with one-point crossover on bits. Bit crossover preserves positions around a cut; subtree crossover preserves hierarchical units. Both encode a hypothesis about what should survive recombination. Operator design is therefore a statement about meaningful modularity.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: Compare this with one-point crossover on bits.

focuses.phrase: Compare this with one-point crossover on bits.
focuses.label: Boundary

segments.label: Transfer and audit
segments.text: After crossover, execute unit tests before expensive fitness evaluation. Catch invalid numeric values, timeouts, and unsafe actions. Evolution is permitted to be imaginative; the sandbox is permitted to be unimpressed and pull the plug.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: After crossover, execute unit tests before expensive

focuses.phrase: After crossover, execute unit tests before expensive
focuses.label: Transfer and audit

slides.title: Fitness-guided inheritance accumulates useful structure

segments.label: Concept
segments.text: The question contrasts evolutionary search with independently random programs. Random generation can occasionally create a good tree, but it does not accumulate discoveries. Every sample forgets what previous samples learned.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: The question contrasts evolutionary search with independently

focuses.phrase: The question contrasts evolutionary search with independently
focuses.label: Concept

segments.label: Mechanism
segments.text: Fitness-based selection creates continuity. Programs containing useful partial structure reproduce more often, allowing mutation and crossover to refine or recombine those parts. Evolution becomes a biased sampling process whose distribution changes with evidence.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: Fitness-based selection creates continuity. Programs containing useful

focuses.phrase: Fitness-based selection creates continuity. Programs containing useful
focuses.label: Mechanism

kinetics.phrase: Fitness-based selection creates continuity. Programs containing useful
kinetics.label: Guided search versus random programs

segments.label: Example and metaphor
segments.text: Trees are not always shorter, random programs can execute, and mutation never guarantees optimality. The correct mechanism is preservation plus variation. A useful building block receives additional trials in related contexts.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: Trees are not always shorter, random programs

focuses.phrase: Trees are not always shorter, random programs
focuses.label: Example and metaphor

segments.label: Boundary
segments.text: The claim still needs conditions. Selection pressure that is too weak resembles random search; pressure that is too strong erases diversity and may lock onto a mediocre family. Cumulative improvement needs both memory of evidence and continued exploration.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: The claim still needs conditions. Selection pressure

focuses.phrase: The claim still needs conditions. Selection pressure
focuses.label: Boundary

segments.label: Transfer and audit
segments.text: Imagine solving a puzzle by keeping promising partial assemblies versus dumping the table after every attempt. Random restart may eventually succeed, but selection lets the algorithm remember that two corner pieces already cooperate. It is less dramatic and much kinder to the carpet.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: Imagine solving a puzzle by keeping promising

focuses.phrase: Imagine solving a puzzle by keeping promising
focuses.label: Transfer and audit

slides.title: Sensors, actions, and control flow become GP primitives

segments.label: Concept
segments.text: In the maze case, programs control a mouse seeking cheese. The function set contains control structures such as IF movement-blocked and WHILE not-at-cheese. Terminals are executable actions such as move forward, turn left, and turn right.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: In the maze case, programs control a

focuses.phrase: In the maze case, programs control a
focuses.label: Concept

segments.label: Mechanism
segments.text: This primitive set embeds domain knowledge. IF movement-blocked gives the controller a relevant sensor; movement actions give it legal effectors. If the language lacks a needed observation or action, no amount of evolution can represent the missing behavior.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: This primitive set embeds domain knowledge. IF

focuses.phrase: This primitive set embeds domain knowledge. IF
focuses.label: Mechanism

kinetics.phrase: This primitive set embeds domain knowledge. IF
kinetics.label: Interactive mouse controller

segments.label: Example and metaphor
segments.text: The displayed program loops until the cheese is reached. When blocked it turns left; otherwise it moves forward. Whether this works depends on maze geometry and execution limits. A loop can navigate, circle forever, or discover that one wall deserves a long-term relationship.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: The displayed program loops until the cheese

focuses.phrase: The displayed program loops until the cheese
focuses.label: Example and metaphor

segments.label: Boundary
segments.text: Sufficiency asks whether the primitives can express successful navigation. Closure asks whether every composition can run. Parsimony asks whether the language and pressure avoid needless complexity. These properties shape the candidate space before fitness begins selecting.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: Sufficiency asks whether the primitives can express

focuses.phrase: Sufficiency asks whether the primitives can express
focuses.label: Boundary

segments.label: Transfer and audit
segments.text: Test controllers on multiple mazes, not only the training layout. A program can memorize one corridor pattern without learning general navigation. Held-out mazes reveal whether the evolved logic transfers when the walls rearrange the furniture.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: Test controllers on multiple mazes, not only

focuses.phrase: Test controllers on multiple mazes, not only
focuses.label: Transfer and audit

segments.label: Mechanism
segments.text: Units spent rewards efficiency; remaining distance gives partial credit when the mouse fails to finish. Squaring magnifies differences among poor outcomes. The formula therefore defines a specific tradeoff, not an objective truth about navigation.

segments.text: One result does not establish an operator hierarchy. Mutation can be neutral because the changed subtree never executes, produces equivalent behavior, or affects a case absent from this maze. Crossover can improve one child and damage another.

slides.title: Sufficiency, parsimony, and closure constrain the search

segments.label: Concept
segments.text: Sufficiency means the primitive set can represent solutions. If the mouse needs to sense a blocked path but no primitive exposes that information, successful reactive navigation may be impossible. The optimum cannot be discovered if the language cannot say it.

focuses.phrase: Sufficiency means the primitive set can represent

segments.label: Mechanism
segments.text: Parsimony favors simpler programs when performance is comparable. Size limits, depth limits, or explicit complexity penalties reduce bloat. Simpler trees are usually cheaper to execute, easier to inspect, and less likely to contain accidental behavior.

focuses.label: Mechanism

segments.label: Example and metaphor
segments.text: Closure means every permitted composition produces a valid executable result. Protected division, typed nodes, and safe action wrappers support closure. Without it, random generation and variation create candidates that crash before fitness can compare them.

slides.title: Steady-state GP replaces sampled losers continuously

segments.label: Concept
segments.text: Tournament GP samples a small subset of the population. Evaluate or compare those programs, select a winner as parent, apply variation, and replace a loser. The population changes incrementally rather than being rebuilt as a whole generation.

focuses.phrase: Tournament GP samples a small subset of

segments.label: Mechanism
segments.text: Tournament size controls selection pressure. A large tournament makes strong programs likely to win; a small tournament preserves more randomness. Replacement policy matters too: replacing the worst sampled member differs from replacing a random member.

segments.label: Example and metaphor
segments.text: Steady-state updates can use evaluations efficiently because each new child immediately enters the population. They also blur generation boundaries, so report progress by evaluation count rather than pretending every arbitrary batch is a biological birthday.

focuses.phrase: Steady-state updates can use evaluations efficiently because

segments.text: Evaporation weakens old trails. Without evaporation, early random choices could dominate forever. Decay preserves exploration and lets the colony adapt when evidence changes. Memory exists in the environment rather than in one ant's private notebook.

slides.title: Exploration, reinforcement, and evaporation create adaptive shared memory

segments.label: Concept
segments.text: The discovery trace begins with random scouts leaving the nest without a reliable trail. Local stochastic motion gives the colony broad coverage. Most scouts fail, but exploration creates the possibility that one ant encounters food.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: The discovery trace begins with random scouts

focuses.phrase: The discovery trace begins with random scouts
focuses.label: Concept

segments.label: Mechanism
segments.text: A successful scout returns while depositing pheromone. The trail is external memory: later ants can sense and follow evidence left in the environment by an agent they never met. This indirect coordination is called stigmergy.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: A successful scout returns while depositing pheromone.

focuses.phrase: A successful scout returns while depositing pheromone.

segments.label: Example and metaphor
segments.text: Followers choose the marked path probabilistically and strengthen it after successful trips. Reinforcement makes useful evidence self-amplifying, while stochastic alternatives remain available long enough to discover a better route.

segments.label: Boundary

slides.title: Match each method to its candidate, feedback, operator, and memory

segments.label: Concept
segments.text: The comparison table begins with the candidate. GA uses a fixed encoding; GP uses a program tree; PSO uses a numerical position and velocity; ACO incrementally constructs a path or combinatorial solution.

segments.label: Mechanism
segments.text: Updates differ. GA uses crossover and mutation, GP uses subtree operators, PSO moves particles using personal and social bests, and ACO changes probabilistic choices through pheromone reinforcement and evaporation.

segments.text: The final claim is compact: complex behavior can emerge from evolving executable structures or repeated local interactions, but the result is governed by representation, feedback, constraints, and evaluation.
